issues.legal_issue: Whether the sellers’ claim that the buyer paid only part of the recorded advance was sufficient to establish that the sale agreement had been cancelled.
material_facts: The written memorandum, signed by both sides, expressly recorded that the sellers had received the full advance.

The sellers later claimed that only part of the recorded advance had been paid and that the balance was due within three days, but there was no contemporaneous written reservation or acknowledgment of an unpaid balance.
The buyer and the document’s writer testified that the full advance had been paid; the court found their account more consistent with the circumstances than the sellers’ account.
The buyer promptly brought a suit for specific performance and deposited the remaining purchase price in court.
issues.conclusion: The sellers’ account that only part of the advance had been paid was untrue; the recorded advance was treated as paid, so the agreement was not cancelled on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: An express recital in a written agreement that payment was received is significant evidence of payment. In the circumstances, the burden lay heavily on the sellers to prove that the recital was false, and the evidence and broad probabilities did not support their account.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and written_agreement_recites_advance_received and sellers_claimed_less_was_paid and no_contemporaneous_written_reservation_of_unpaid_balance and buyer_promptly_deposited_remaining_price

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The buyer brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.written_agreement_recites_advance_receiv: The signed sale memorandum stated that the sellers had received the recorded advance payment.
predicates.sellers_claimed_less_was_paid: The sellers later claimed that the buyer had paid less than the amount recorded as received.
predicates.no_contemporaneous_written_reservation_o: When the sellers delivered the memorandum, they made no written record that part of the advance remained unpaid.
predicates.buyer_promptly_deposited_remaining_price: The buyer promptly deposited the remaining purchase price in court.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance proceeding concerns a recorded advance, the sellers claim less was paid, there was no contemporaneous written reservation of an unpaid balance, and the buyer promptly deposited the remainder, the recorded advance is treated as paid.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a post-execution addition stating that the seller must clear encumbrances makes a sale agreement invalid as a material alteration.
material_facts: The sellers alleged that words requiring clearance of debts and transfer free from encumbrances were added to the memorandum after it was executed.
The court considered the addition even on the assumption that it had been made after execution.
The sale agreement concerned land, and the court held that the seller would ordinarily be responsible for clearing any encumbrances before executing the sale deed.
The court found that the added words did not change the parties’ rights or liabilities or the legal effect of the agreement.
issues.conclusion: The alleged addition was not a material alteration and did not invalidate the agreement.
issues.legal_principle: A post-execution alteration is material if it varies the parties’ rights, liabilities, or legal position, changes the instrument’s legal effect, or otherwise prejudices a party bound by it. An alteration that merely states an obligation already implied by law is not material. The Court relied on Halsbury’s Laws of England, Articles 599 and 604, and applied the principle in Nathu Lal v. Mussamat Gomti Kuar, L.R. 67 I.A. 318.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.alleged_post_execution_addition: A party alleged that a term was added to the written agreement after it was executed.
predicates.added_term_only_expresses_existing_vendo: The added term stated an obligation the seller already had in relation to transferring the property.
predicates.addition_does_not_change_parties_legal_p: The addition did not vary either party’s rights or liabilities, change the agreement’s legal effect, or prejudice a party bound by it.

issues.definition: If a term is alleged to have been added after execution but merely expresses the seller’s existing obligation and does not alter either party’s legal position, the agreement remains valid despite the addition.
